costGuide.title: Ford 4HV Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Ford 4HV typically takes 8-11 hours at an independent specialist rate of £65/hr, resulting in a typical fitted premium of £520-£715 . Confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The final cost of a 4HV replacement is heavily influenced by the condition of the turbocharger and fuel injectors, which are common wear items on high-mileage commercial units. A proper reconditioned 4HV will include new or refurbished piezoelectric injectors, a cleaned or replaced DPF, and updated turbo seals. Always verify that the EGR system has been addressed, as carbon buildup is a primary driver of replacement demand. For a full breakdown of market rates and condition tiers, see our reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: Ford 4HV Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector Failure and Fuel System Contamination - 2006-2016 units
items.whatHappens: The 4HV's piezoelectric injectors are susceptible to wear and carbon buildup, particularly in vehicles subjected to frequent short trips or poor-quality diesel. Symptoms include rough idling, excessive black smoke, difficulty starting, and a noticeable loss of power. If an injector leaks, it can wash down the cylinder walls, diluting the engine oil and leading to rapid bearing wear.
items.repairVsReplace: While a single faulty injector can be replaced, it is common for multiple injectors to fail in sequence on high-mileage units. If oil dilution has occurred, a full engine replacement is often the most reliable and cost-effective long-term solution. Read our full injector failure guide.

items.title: DPF Clogging and EGR Valve Issues
items.whatHappens: As a commercial vehicle, the 4HV is frequently used in urban environments with stop-start driving, which prevents the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) from reaching the temperatures required for active regeneration. This leads to progressive clogging, triggering engine management lights and forcing the vehicle into "limp mode". Concurrently, the EGR valve can become clogged with soot, exacerbating the issue.
items.repairVsReplace: A DPF clean or EGR service can provide temporary relief. However, if the clogging has caused excessive backpressure, it can lead to turbocharger failure or piston damage, necessitating a full unit replacement. Read our full DPF failure guide.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 4HV is generally considered a robust commercial engine when maintained with strict oil change intervals and high-quality diesel, though urban-only use significantly accelerates DPF and EGR degradation .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 4HV
variants.intro: The 4HV engine code is stamped directly onto the engine block, typically located on a machined pad near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code" and can be independently verified via a VIN decode.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 4HV - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 4HV is a viable option for budget-conscious fleet operators, provided the unit comes with a verifiable service history and no history of DPF-related limp mode or injector failure. Given the commercial nature of the host vehicles, mileage verification is critical to avoid inheriting a unit near the end of its service life. Explore used Ford engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 4HV is the most recommended path for most owners. A reputable rebuild will address the core weaknesses by fitting new or refurbished piezoelectric injectors, cleaning or replacing the DPF, and renewing all turbocharger seals and EGR components. This resolves the dominant failure patterns while keeping costs well below a full custom rebuild. Explore reconditioned Ford engines.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the original 4HV suffered catastrophic failure due to severe oil dilution from a leaking injector or a seized turbocharger sending debris into the oil galleries. An upgraded rebuild should include new pistons, a machined block, and an updated oil pump to prevent future lubrication issues. Explore rebuilt Ford engines.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network of vetted UK commercial vehicle specialists can supply the 4HV unit and handle the complete installation, including ECU adaptation and DPF regeneration cycles, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty. Learn more about supply & fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 4HV is typically found in Ford Transit and Ranger models valued between £2,000 and £8,000 depending on age, mileage, and specification. If your vehicle is at the lower end of this spectrum (e.g., an early 2006-2008 Transit with over 150,000 miles), a £1,500+ reconditioned engine replacement may approach or exceed 60% of the van's current market value. In these specific scenarios, it is financially prudent to evaluate the vehicle's scrap or part-exchange value first. However, for well-maintained, higher-value examples, investing in a properly reconditioned 4HV remains a cost-effective alternative to vehicle replacement.

items.question: How much does a Ford 4HV engine replacement cost in the UK?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ford 4HV engine costs between £1,500 and £2,800 for supply only, or £2,020 to £3,515 fully fitted by an independent specialist. Used units start around £500 but carry high-mileage commercial risks. Labour typically adds a £520-£715 premium to the supply cost.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the Ford 4HV 2.2 TDCi?
items.answer: The dominant failures are piezoelectric injector wear and DPF clogging, typically emerging between 80,000 and 150,000 miles. Symptoms include rough idling, excessive black smoke, and limp mode from restricted exhaust flow. Ignoring injector leaks leads to oil dilution and catastrophic bearing failure.

items.question: Which Ford models use the 4HV engine?
items.answer: The 4HV 2.2L Duratorq TDCi was fitted to the Ford Transit (Mk7/Mk8) and Ford Ranger (Mk2) from 2006 to 2016. It serves as the primary commercial workhorse diesel across these vans and pickups. Always verify your specific chassis via registration lookup before ordering.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 4HV engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned 4HV is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high risk of latent injector and DPF failures in high-mileage commercial vehicles. A proper recon includes refurbished piezoelectric injectors, a cleaned or replaced DPF, and renewed turbo seals. A used unit may simply pass the same commercial downtime risk to your fleet.

items.question: How do I know if my van has the 4HV engine code?
items.answer: The 4HV code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover, and is listed on your V5C document. It is frequently confused with the 4HC (different tune) or older 2.0L Duratorq codes like FA or FC. Fitting the wrong revision causes ECU mapping conflicts and loom incompatibility.
